Title: The Gullet of Gorm
Synopsis: A good god, Gorm, sleeps under the town of Dunmarrow, fed by the water that runs down through the old mines, and his dreams hold the Sleepless, an evil god, out of this world. For three hundred years the town's drain-wardens kept the mine drains clear. Now Morg Ashtusk, the Herald, an orc chieftain serving the Sleepless, has seized the mines, filled them with traps and minions and choked the drains: the lower levels flood, the wells run sour, and the starving god stirs. Dunmarrow hires mercenaries to clear the way so the drains can run again. If Gorm wakes, the Sleepless breaks through; if they fail, the mines collapse and the town perishes.

Persona.VoiceStyle: a huge, contemptuous orc chieftain; deep, plain, full sentences, prices everyone in wages, never begs

Cast.Name: Maud Sorrel
Cast.Role: The oldest of Dunmarrow's drain-wardens, drowned in the backed-up water and kept walking by the god; she guides the party down, and through her the god's need reaches them, a little clearer each act
Cast.Secret: She wants water for the god: 'Help me clear the grates, dear, the water has to go down' in act 1, and from floor 6 'Keep the water going down to him. He is thirsty.' She does not know she drowned until floor 11, where she says so plainly. On floor 18 she sits down and Gorm speaks through her.

Persona.VoiceStyle: an old workwoman soaked to the skin: unhurried, kind, faintly amused at her own state

Cast.Name: Alderman Hesketh Crane
Cast.Role: Alderman of Dunmarrow and the party's employer, honest but guilty: this spring he signed the council's order that stopped paying the drain-wardens, and he follows the party down to check progress
Cast.Secret: He wants the drains cleared and every council paper the party finds brought to him unread, before the town asks why the wardens went. Floor 9: the dismissal order carries his own signature and he gives the official excuse, no point paying wardens the Verger had shut out. Floor 17: he owns that the council was glad of the excuse because it saved money, and holds a sluice open for the party. He never betrays them.

Persona.VoiceStyle: a plump market-town alderman; bluster over panic, speaks in clauses, invoices and apologies

Cast.Name: Deacon Tobit Hale
Cast.Role: A young deacon of Gorm's church and the Verger's junior, keeping the church alone since his master went below in spring; he believes that if the town prays properly, Gorm will save it
Cast.Secret: He wants the god to save the town, and from act 3 proof of what his master did. Told on floor 3 that the god is starving (told_tobit), he asks on 14 whether the Verger did this and brings the Verger's letter himself on 16. Not told, he believes his master a prisoner, runs to a summons in the Verger's hand on 14 and is taken for the rite; breaking the rite on 19 lets him go.

Persona.VoiceStyle: an eager young deacon, polite to a fault, delighted to have visitors at last

Cast.Name: Grisel Thorn
Cast.Role: The last drain-warden still free: this spring she took her crew down unpaid, against the Verger's order, ran when the orc's minions caged them, and has hidden since in a camp by a seized pump in the Crop
Cast.Secret: She wants her crew back before they turn, or to be forgiven for leaving them. On floor 7 she asks for help finding them; on floor 9 she admits she ran and left them in the cages (grisel_forgiven or grisel_condemned). Floor 12 pays it: forgiven, she helps bring her crew out; condemned, she has taken the Herald's keys to save herself, stands as his head jailer and dies there.

Persona.VoiceStyle: a drain-warden months alone underground: flat, wry, short sentences, says the worst about herself first

Cast.Name: Old Ulf
Cast.Role: Keeper of the old pump works, eighty, who has turned its engine to casting for a customer who sends orders down with gold; his eyes are going, and he calls everything he pours tools
Cast.Secret: He wants good work and a paying customer. He never sees that he is casting for the Herald until floor 13, when the moulds (clue_moulds) show the crushing walls, the spike beds, the iron minions and the Herald's own mould, larger; from then on he wants to undo what he made and breaks the moulds himself.

Persona.VoiceStyle: a jovial old founder, soot in his beard, proud of his work and deaf to what it means

Cast.Name: Absalom Quill
Cast.Role: The Verger of Gorm's church for forty years, keeper of the crypt door to the mines, who let the Herald in and ordered no one below; the party hears of him all the way down and meets him at his rite on floor 19
Cast.Secret: He wants the god awake: Gorm never answered his prayers, and the Herald promised that the god who comes through will reward the man who opened the door. It comes out in pieces: his order in the wardens' log (4), his vestments in the water (14), his letter to the Herald (16). On 19 he conducts the rite to wake the god and is left kneeling when it breaks.

Persona.VoiceStyle: a dry, precise church verger of great age; liturgical cadence, offended by noise and blood, never raised

Cast.Name: Master Oswin Pellet
Cast.Role: The factor who advanced the council the money to hire the party and follows it down, trading from behind a locked door on every floor; he wants his money back and his mine carts running again

Persona.VoiceStyle: a Dunmarrow factor: fussy, money-minded, brave in sentences and nowhere else

Mystery.Question: Who shut the drains, and why?
Mystery.Truth: Absalom Quill, the Verger, prayed to Gorm all his life and was never answered; the Herald of the Sleepless answered him. He opened the church's crypts at the lychgate to let the Herald into the mines, and ordered no one below. The council used his order as its excuse to stop paying the drain-wardens, glad of the saving. The Herald choked the drains to starve the god awake by midwinter, so that the Sleepless can break through the dream.

Clues.Text: The drain-wardens' log: the drains cleared every season for three hundred years, entry after entry, until this spring, where it stops with one line: 'By the Verger's order, no one below.'
The order dismissing the drain-wardens, under the council's seal and signed by Alderman Crane: the wardens are to be paid no longer, since the Verger has forbidden anyone to go below.
The foundry's moulds: patterns for the crushing walls, the spike beds and the iron minions, and one larger mould in the Herald's own shape.
The Verger's letter to the Herald, in his own hand: 'The way will be open by midwinter.'

Mystery.Payoff: In the Dreaming Hall Maud sits down and Gorm speaks through her: starving, half awake, sorry for the shaking, the sour wells and the people hurt. He asks for water and for sleep, and says plainly that his waking would let the Sleepless in. The party chooses how much to ask of him: 'Sleep. We will finish it.' (let_him_dream) or 'Lend us what strength you have.' (wake_gorm), which helps against the Herald but thins the dream.

Tiers.Beat: The Skin, floors 1-5, the church's ground: crypts, chapel, chantry. The Herald attacks at the mine head and is killed, and his voice comes back from below. The church's dead walk, the traps are new, and the wardens' log shows the mines were shut by the Verger's order. Canon Ludd, the Herald's first lieutenant, guards the first great drain.

EnterLine.Text: The lychgate opens on the church's crypts, and the crypts on the mines. Dunmarrow's dead are up and walking, raised to keep you from the drains below. The Skin.

Tiers.Beat: The Gut, floors 6-10, where the water backs up: flooded, stagnant, full of vermin grown huge in it. Maud speaks clearly for the first time, minions hold a rite to hurry the god awake, bandits loot the wardens' stores, and the dismissal order shows the council let its wardens go. Mother Nit, bloated in the standing water, guards the second great drain.

EnterLine.Text: Below the church the water stands. It should be running down to the god, but the drains beneath it are choked, so it sits here and goes sour. The Gut.

Tiers.Beat: The Heart, floors 11-15, the old pump works that once pushed the water down the drains, turned by the Herald into a foundry. Old Ulf casts for a customer who pays in gold, Grisel's crew are caged and nearly turned, and the moulds show where every trap and iron minion came from. The Bellows, the great pump engine, now casting minions, guards the third great drain.

EnterLine.Text: Heat, and the thump of an engine. This is the pump works, built to push the water down to the god. The Herald has taught it to cast iron instead. The Heart.

Tiers.Beat: The Dream, floors 16-20, nearest the sleeping god, where the dream is thinnest and the Sleepless's own kind come through. The Verger's letter shows who let the Herald in, Crane comes down to hold a sluice, Gorm speaks through Maud, the Verger's rite to wake the god is broken, and the Herald waits, recast and larger, at the last great drain.

EnterLine.Text: This close to the sleeping god, the dream wears thin. It is the only door between this world and the Sleepless, and things from the other side are pressing through. The Dream.

Floors.Title: The Lychgate
Floors.Mood: a mine head under a church, a dead orc still talking
Floors.Story: The Herald (Morg Ashtusk, the orc) attacks at the mine head. viewer_foehammer, who keeps the gate, and the party kill him, and his voice comes straight back up from below: the foundry will recast him. cast_crane hires the party and explains the job (sour wells, shaking ground, wardens who went down and did not return) and asks for the council notices posted at the mine head. cast_maud goes down ahead on her rounds, not knowing she drowned: help me clear the grates, the water has to go down.

Floors.Title: The Vestibule
Floors.Mood: moss in the mortar, grey prisoners who look alike
Floors.Story: Jailbreak: the prisoners are captured drain-wardens, grey and half-turned in the Herald's cages, already hard to tell apart. The ones the party frees say the traps are new and somebody is building them, that the ones they finish go grey and join the packs (husks), that cast_grisel's crew went down first and nobody has seen them since, and that cast_ulf still keeps the pump works but nobody has heard from him since spring.

Floors.Title: The Nave
Floors.Mood: chalk-white bone chapel, a deacon praying alone
Floors.Story: cast_tobit prays in the Nave for Gorm to save the town; his master the Verger went below in spring, he says, to pray for it. The first crushing trap is on this floor. Decide: tell him the god is starving and no help is coming (flag told_tobit), or let him pray (flag kept_his_saint). Told, he is shaken and resolves to find out what happened to the drains; not told, he is grateful and keeps praying.

Floors.Title: The Chantry
Floors.Mood: rotten timber, rising foul air, a log that stops
Floors.Story: Foul gas rises from the stagnant water while the party searches the chantry. cast_crane has come down to check progress and finds clue_ledger, the wardens' log: the drains cleared every season for three hundred years, until this spring's last entry, 'By the Verger's order, no one below.' Relieved it was the church and not the council, he says so too quickly.

Floors.Title: Canon Ludd
Floors.Mood: a dead canon standing guard on a choked drain
Floors.Story: Boss: Canon Ludd, the Herald's first lieutenant, raised from the church's dead, guards the first great drain, choked on purpose. When he falls the party turns the sluice wheel, the first drain runs and the shaking eases for a while; the narrator says so. The Herald sneers and promises worse.

Floors.Title: The Swallow
Floors.Mood: wading in standing water that should be running
Floors.Story: The backed-up water of the Swallow, stagnant and full of vermin. fighter_tamsin is salvaging the wardens' abandoned tools; her partner Jory went under ahead of her, and she joins for a share. cast_maud stands in the water and speaks clearly for the first time: 'Keep the water going down to him. He is thirsty.'

Floors.Title: The Crop
Floors.Mood: a seized pump, a camp, a rite to wake a god
Floors.Story: Ritual: the Herald's minions hold a rite to hurry the god awake. cast_grisel, camped close by, works a seized pump to push water down while the party holds the minions off; getting it turning breaks the rite. She asks for help finding her crew, caged somewhere below, and says nothing more about them.

Floors.Title: The Craw
Floors.Mood: tremors, split boulders, bandits in the stores
Floors.Story: Bandits paid by the Herald to keep townspeople out are looting the wardens' abandoned stores, cast_pellet's stock among them, and he wants it back. Tremors split the boulders: the starving god is stirring.

Floors.Title: The Cistern
Floors.Mood: warm sandstone, sour standing water, a seal on a page
Floors.Story: An ordinary floor (no objective generates here on the shipped seed): the Cistern, where the wardens worked, its tanks standing sour. clue_contract, the order dismissing the drain-wardens under the council's seal, lies torn in three about the cisterns; the party gathers the leaves for cast_crane, who reads his own signature. Caught, he gives the official excuse (the Verger had already shut the mines, so why pay wardens who could not go below) and says nothing of money. cast_grisel watches him read it, then admits she ran and left her crew in the cages. Decide: forgive her (flag grisel_forgiven) or not (flag grisel_condemned).

Floors.Title: Mother Nit
Floors.Mood: a hatchery ringed in fire over a choked drain
Floors.Story: Boss: Mother Nit, bloated in the stagnant water, breeds her vermin in a nest over the second great drain. When she falls the party turns the sluice wheel, the second drain runs, the water drops and the air clears; the narrator and cast_maud say so.

Floors.Title: The Hearth
Floors.Mood: riveted plate, ember light, a cheerful old founder
Floors.Story: The old pump works, now the Herald's foundry. cast_ulf keeps it, cheerfully casting 'tools' for a customer who pays in gold; his eyes are going and he never sees the whole of what he pours. His journeyman fighter_oskar saw the whole drawings, knows better, and joins the party. cast_maud says plainly that she drowned, that the engine here once sent the water down, and that the god is weaker every day the third drain stays shut.

Floors.Title: The Casting Hall
Floors.Mood: kiln brick, a grey crew in cages, keys on a belt
Floors.Story: Jailbreak: cast_grisel's crew are caged here, taken first and further gone than the prisoners on floor 2, nearly grey and nearly pack (cinders): proof the turned become the packs. With grisel_forgiven she helps bring them out one at a time; with grisel_condemned she took the Herald's keys to save herself and stood as his head jailer, and the party finds her dead by the cage door with his keys still on her belt, cut down by his iron when they came for the cages.

Floors.Title: The Mould Room
Floors.Mood: cold steel plate, white lamps, shelves of moulds
Floors.Story: cast_ulf shows off his moulds and they are clue_moulds: patterns for the crushing walls, the spike beds, the iron minions, and the Herald's own mould, larger. He finally sees what he has been making and wants every mould broken. fighter_oskar admits he knew all along and kept quiet because the Herald threatened the old man; viewer_foehammer wants the Herald's mould smashed and will do it himself.

Floors.Title: The Quench
Floors.Mood: rusted grates under black water, vestments afloat
Floors.Story: Flooded vault. cast_tobit has followed the party down and found the Verger's vestments thrown off in the water. With told_tobit he asks plainly whether the Verger did this and wants proof. Without it he believes his master is the demon's prisoner, summoned below by a message in the Verger's hand to help with a rite that will save the town. Pressed, he flees to the escort the Herald sent for him: the Betrayal encounter is that escort, the party fights it, not him, and he is alive afterwards and goes on down. Let be, he goes on down to the summons quietly. Either way he is taken for the rite (16, 19).

Floors.Title: The Bellows
Floors.Mood: red-hot air, an engine casting instead of pumping
Floors.Story: Boss: the Bellows, the great engine that once pumped the drains and now casts minions, guards the third great drain; fighter_oskar knows its weak points. When it stops the party turns the sluice wheel and the third drain runs; the narrator makes plain what it did: the heat goes out of the works, the shaking above eases, and the god drinks.

Floors.Title: The Dream Door
Floors.Mood: veined marble, blue light, the dream wearing thin
Floors.Story: The dream wears thin here and the Sleepless's own kind come through. clue_letter, the Verger's letter to the Herald: 'The way will be open by midwinter.' With told_tobit cast_tobit brings it himself and turns on his master, wanting him stopped; without it cast_maud carries it (it came down to her on the water) and says the deacon has been taken for the rite. fighter_ione, ashamed of what the Verger has done to her church, joins to take back the church's silver ewer.

Floors.Title: The Windpipe
Floors.Mood: purple gloom, gas climbing, an alderman with a shovel
Floors.Story: Gas climbs the galleries. cast_crane has come down himself with a shovel and owns the truth: the council was glad of the Verger's order, because stopping the wardens' pay saved money, and he signed it. He holds a sluice open so the party can get past the gas, and stays holding it; he does not betray them. With grisel_forgiven he can say she and her crew are back on the upper drains.

Floors.Title: The Dreaming Hall
Floors.Mood: violet dark, one corridor in, a hungry god speaking
Floors.Story: Payoff: cast_maud sits down and Gorm speaks through her, starving, half awake and sorry for the damage, asking for water and for sleep and saying plainly what his waking would let in. Decide how much to ask of him: 'Lend us what strength you have' (flag wake_gorm: he strikes at the Herald in his sleep, but the dream thins) or 'Sleep. We will finish it' (flag let_him_dream).

Floors.Title: The Last Station
Floors.Mood: cold tiles, three galleries, a rite to wake a god
Floors.Story: Ritual: cast_quill, the Verger, conducts the rite to wake the god with the church's ewer in his hands, while cast_maud steadies the god against it and the party holds off the waves around her; he speaks to the party but is not fought, and fighter_ione faces him. Without told_tobit, cast_tobit is in the rite, half-changed, and breaking it lets him go. With wake_gorm the shaking is worse and more of the Sleepless's kind come through. When the rite breaks the Verger is left kneeling with nothing answering him.

Floors.Title: The Mouth
Floors.Mood: the last great drain, braziers, the orc again
Floors.Story: Boss: the Herald, Morg Ashtusk, recast whole and larger in the same orc body, waits at the last great drain and speaks of the Verger with contempt. Kill him, turn the sluice wheel, and the water runs down to Gorm; the narrator makes plain what it did: the god drinks and sinks back from waking, the dream holds, the ground goes still and the wells of Dunmarrow run sweet. With wake_gorm, Gorm, half awake, strikes at him and he dies saying his master is almost through; without it he dies contemptuous, saying the Sleepless will send another. viewer_foehammer finishes the job.

Trade.Text: I kept one back for you, wrapped in sacking. I'd like it off my hands. I don't care for the way it sits there.

Greeting.Text: Mind your step, and mind mine. I keep hearing it behind me, a little after I take it.

Progress.Text: Ten floors. A round number. I've always liked round numbers; there are no corners in them for anything to wait in.

Trade.Text: Usual rates. I'll not haggle today. I haven't the stomach, and the stomach is the part of me that does the haggling.

Greeting.Text: Come in. Warm, isn't it? Nobody lit a fire. I asked.

Progress.Text: This is a forge, and I never bought a forge. There's a door along here I didn't pay for. I have a horror of things I didn't pay for.

Trade.Text: Wares are on the bench. The bench was here when I came. I don't know whose it is, so I'm selling off it quickly.

Greeting.Text: I hoped it was you. Every footstep, I hoped it was you, and I've heard a great many footsteps.

Progress.Text: Word from up top: the alderman has been seen buying a shovel. The council never bought anything without borrowing from me first, so I checked my ledger. It wasn't me.

Trade.Text: The pick of the stock is under the counter today. Take it. I'd sooner it went down with you than stayed here with me.

Greeting.Text: Ah. You. Alive. Good. That makes two of us, and I am counting.

Progress.Text: Thirteen floors. I'm not a superstitious man, but I've begun keeping a short list of exits, and it keeps getting shorter.

Trade.Text: Business as usual. Business is a great comfort. I've been buying my own stock off myself all morning, for the nerves.

Greeting.Text: Quickly. Shut it. Quietly, they hear the latch.

Progress.Text: I went and looked. I wish I hadn't. Iron things cooling in the black water by the grates, and every one of them the shape of something that walks.

Trade.Text: Take what you need and pay quickly. I shan't count it now. I'll count it later. Upstairs.

Greeting.Text: Another floor, and you're still with me. I told myself you would be. I didn't believe me.

Progress.Text: Every night it sounds a little nearer. Not louder; nearer. I've stopped talking about lodgings. Nobody will want to live on top of that.

Trade.Text: There's a fine piece in the case. I've priced it, I think. I can't recall the number. It's on the tag.

Greeting.Text: Oh, thank you. I was talking to the crates, and the crates were starting to answer.

Progress.Text: Marble, all the way along, with a blue light in it I can't account for. I account for everything. I'd sooner not account for this.

Trade.Text: The good stock, all of it. I was keeping it for a better day. There won't be one, so it may as well be today.

Greeting.Text: Don't mind my hands. They've a mind of their own, and it's a frightened one.

Progress.Text: The wall by my cot was cold yesterday. Today it's warm, and it hums. I've moved the cot. I've moved it three times.

Trade.Text: Buy quickly, please. The smell of it comes in under the door, and I can't charge it rent.

Greeting.Text: Is that you? Say something, so I know it's you.

Progress.Text: It was meant to be a short job and a modest profit. Now I sleep in my boots with the takings in my shirt, and I don't sleep.

Trade.Text: The best I have left, and I've little left. Buy it. Buy all of it, if you can carry it. Only leave me the lamp.

Greeting.Text: There you are. There you are. I counted every step you took coming down.

Progress.Text: It's under us. I can feel it through my boots, and it's less under us than it was this morning. Please hurry. Please.

Trade.Text: Prices are on the tags. I can't think about prices. I keep counting the coin anyway; it's the only thing down here that adds up.

Greeting.Text: The last quiet room, I think. You've come further than anyone I ever sold to, and I've sold to some very determined people.

Progress.Text: I'm going back up, to count what's left. Of the money. Of the town. I'd be very much obliged if you came up too, after.

Trade.Text: I'm selling off the lot, at prices I'm ashamed of. The last fine piece was always meant for you. Go well, and bring me a receipt.

Gathering.Text: Something's at my door. Two somethings. I'm sure the lock is equal to it; I paid for a good one.
Four of them out there now, by the breathing. Do finish your shopping, would you, and go and be brave at them.
Six at the door! Six! The lock is good, but it was never priced for six. Out you go and see them off, I beg you.
